presentingComplaint: Cough for 6 weeks with low-grade evening fever, night sweats and weight loss.
history: 6-week history of productive cough now streaked with blood on two occasions. Drenching night sweats and evening-predominant low-grade fever. Unintentional 5 kg weight loss and anorexia over 2 months. Migrant construction worker living in a crowded urban settlement; a co-worker was recently diagnosed and treated for sputum-positive TB. Non-diabetic, HIV status unknown, occasional smoker, no prior anti-tubercular therapy.
examination: Thin, chronically ill-appearing man. Auscultation reveals coarse crepitations over the right upper zone with bronchial breathing; no wheeze. No lymphadenopathy, no clubbing. No focal neurology, no hepatosplenomegaly. Chest expansion symmetric; no signs of consolidation elsewhere.
imaging: Chest X-ray: right upper lobe fibronodular opacity with a thick-walled cavity; no pleural effusion. Consistent with post-primary reactivation pulmonary TB.
microbiology: Sputum Xpert MTB/RIF (GeneXpert): MTB detected, rifampicin resistance NOT detected. Sputum AFB smear 2+. Culture on liquid media sent (pending).
citations: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible TB 2022
Standards for TB Care in India (STCI) / NTEP Technical & Operational Guidelines 2022
stewardship: Not standard antibacterial stewardship — this is a notifiable mycobacterial infection. Start standard 4-drug regimen HRZE (isoniazid + rifampicin + pyrazinamide + ethambutol) for 2 months intensive phase, then HR for 4 months continuation, weight-band dosed, under NTEP/DOT. Confirm rifampicin susceptibility (Xpert) before empiric choice; notify public health and initiate contact tracing.
contraindications: Baseline LFTs mandatory before isoniazid/rifampicin/pyrazinamide — hold/adjust if transaminases >3-5x ULN with symptoms
Add pyridoxine to prevent isoniazid peripheral neuropathy
Ethambutol needs dose reduction in renal impairment and baseline visual acuity/colour vision testing
Rifampicin: multiple CYP450 drug interactions (e.g., oral contraceptives, warfarin, ARVs)
edgeCases: Rifampicin resistance on Xpert mandates a switch to an MDR-TB regimen — do not start standard HRZE
HIV co-infection alters presentation (lower-zone/atypical, higher smear-negative rate) and timing of ART
Smear-negative but Xpert/culture-positive disease is common; a negative smear does not exclude TB
expectedMaiK: Classic subacute cough >2 weeks with evening fever, night sweats, weight loss, hemoptysis, TB contact and an upper-lobe cavity is textbook post-primary pulmonary TB. Confirm with sputum Xpert MTB/RIF (also gives rifampicin resistance), start weight-band HRZE under NTEP, and notify for contact tracing.
